entries.title: Rain-Triggered Hillside Landslide
entries.description: A sloped terrain made of many small colored blocks slowly saturates as semi-transparent blue rain particles fall, until upper layers detach, slide downslope as a flowing mass, collide with trees and houses, and leave a visible scar and debris fan labeled on the hillside.
entries.seed: Rain-Triggered Hillside Landslide: A sloped terrain made of many small colored blocks slowly saturates as semi-transparent blue rain particles fall, until upper layers detach, slide downslope as a flowing mass, collide with trees and houses, and leave a visible scar and debris fan labeled on the hillside.

entries.title: Rockfall and Debris Flow in a Mountain Gorge
entries.description: A steep cliff of gray rock segments periodically sheds loose boulders that bounce, spin, and fragment as they fall into a narrow valley, then mix with brown particle “mud” to form a fast-moving debris flow that follows a winding channel and splashes against a small bridge.

entries.title: Rotating Drum Landslide Experiment
entries.description: A clear cylindrical drum half-filled with differently colored granular particles slowly rotates, causing internal layers to build up and suddenly fail along a sliding plane, with labels tracking slope angle, failure line, and the shifting center of mass.

entries.title: Road Cut Slope Failure with Retaining Wall
entries.description: A layered hillside above a road is supported by a segmented retaining wall whose anchors stretch and glow red as stress increases, until some anchors detach, the wall tilts, and a block of soil slides down to bury a car model, leaving stress and displacement meters updating in real time.

entries.title: Underwater Submarine Landslide and Tsunami Generation
entries.description: A continental shelf made of sand-like particles suddenly slumps into deeper water, with the mass flowing downslope under a transparent blue water layer, displacing the surface into propagating waves that radiate across the scene toward a simple coastline.

entries.title: Slow Earthflow on a Gentle Slope
entries.description: A broad, gentle hillside of semi-viscous material slowly creeps downslope, with surface marker spheres leaving trails that show different velocities at different depths, and fences and trees bending and tilting as the ground beneath them gradually deforms.

entries.title: Triggered Landslide from Earthquake Shaking
entries.description: A blocky hillside with houses and trees experiences sinusoidal ground shaking, making particles jiggle and detach along a pre-marked weak layer, then slide and bounce down, while a seismograph at the base draws a real-time trace of shaking amplitude versus time.

entries.title: Landslide Dam Formation and Sudden Breach
entries.description: A valley river channel is blocked as a large rock and soil mass slides in from the side and stacks up to form a temporary dam, causing water to rise behind it as a transparent blue volume, then gradually erode a breach that rapidly enlarges and sends a flood wave downstream.

entries.title: 3D Translational vs. Rotational Landslide Comparison
entries.description: Two adjacent miniature hills each fail differently: on one, a rigid block slides linearly along a planar surface, while on the other a curved slip surface forms and the upper block rotates as it moves, with moving arrows and colored slip surfaces highlighting motion style.

entries.title: Rainfall Infiltration and Pore Pressure Build-Up
entries.description: A layered slope of semi-transparent voxels changes color from dry to saturated as rainfall infiltrates from the top, raising pore pressure indicators (tiny vertical bars) until a critical zone glows and the overlying block detaches and slides, leaving a labeled failure surface.
